story.title: Bryan Cranston Pays Tribute to RJ Mitte Following His Death at 34
story.summary: Bryan Cranston expressed deep sorrow over the death of his 'Breaking Bad' co-star RJ Mitte, who passed away at the age of 34. Cranston referred to Mitte as 'my sweet son' and revealed they had been planning to meet for lunch shortly before his death. Mitte's representative confirmed that he died by suicide at his home in Brownsville, Texas.

explore_lenses.label: What is confirmed, and what remains unresolved?
explore_lenses.title: Representative statement versus official inquiry
explore_lenses.summary: Mitte's representative has publicly identified suicide as the cause of death, while reporting also indicates that Brownsville police had an active investigation and had not publicly issued a final cause-and-manner determination at the time of the initial reports.

claims.text: Mitte's representative told Fox News Digital that suicide was the cause of death; the report said he died at his Brownsville home on Monday.

Reporting attributed to the Brownsville Police Department said officers received a call at 12:50 p.m. local time and that the cause and manner of death remained pending during an ongoing investigation.
Cameron County Justice of the Peace Cyndi Hinojosa told the Associated Press that Mitte was pronounced dead at about 1:30 p.m. Monday in Brownsville.

explore_lenses.label: Why did Mitte matter beyond “Breaking Bad”?
explore_lenses.title: A visible advocate for disability inclusion
explore_lenses.summary: Mitte's public significance extended beyond his television role: he drew on his own cerebral palsy experience in portraying Walter White Jr. and used his prominence in disability-focused advocacy and philanthropy.

claims.text: Mitte's representative said his lived experience with cerebral palsy brought authenticity to Walter White Jr. and helped him build a platform around disability awareness and inclusion.
United Cerebral Palsy lists Mitte as an honorary trustee and describes him as an activist for people with cerebral palsy.

Shriners Hospitals for Children named Mitte a national campaign ambassador in 2014; the organization said he would share his experience receiving cerebral-palsy treatment and encourage support for children with disabilities.

explore_lenses.label: Where can people affected by this news turn?
explore_lenses.title: Crisis support is available now
explore_lenses.summary: Coverage of a suicide can be distressing for people who knew the person, identify with the circumstances, or are already struggling. The U.S. 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline offers immediate, confidential support.

claims.text: The 988 Lifeline says people can call, text, or chat for free and confidential, judgment-free crisis support.
The service offers Spanish call, text, and chat options; callers can dial 988 and press 2 for a Spanish-speaking counselor.
For an immediate physical safety threat or medical emergency, the 988 Lifeline directs people to call 911.

story_report.summary: RJ Mitte, the “Breaking Bad” actor, has died at 34, prompting Bryan Cranston to mourn his former co-star as “my sweet son.” Mitte’s representative told Fox News Digital that suicide was the cause of death and said he died at his Brownsville, Texas, home on Monday. The death drew tributes while the official status of the investigation remained unresolved, with police reporting that the cause and manner of death were still pending.

sections.heading: Brownsville Investigation and Reported Cause
sections.body: Reporting attributed to the Brownsville Police Department said officers received a call at 12:50 p.m. local time. Cameron County Justice of the Peace Cyndi Hinojosa told the Associated Press that Mitte was pronounced dead at about 1:30 p.m. Monday in Brownsville. His representative’s account of suicide has been reported separately from the pending official determination.

sections.heading: RJ Mitte’s Disability Advocacy Work
sections.body: Mitte’s representative said his experience living with cerebral palsy brought authenticity to his portrayal of Walter White Jr. and helped him develop a platform focused on disability awareness and inclusion. United Cerebral Palsy lists him as an honorary trustee and activist, while Shriners Hospitals for Children named him a national campaign ambassador in 2014 to share his treatment experience and encourage support for children with disabilities.

sections.heading: Crisis Support Through 988 Lifeline
sections.body: The 988 Lifeline offers free, confidential and judgment-free crisis support by call, text or chat. Spanish-language support is available by calling 988 and pressing 2, as well as through Spanish text and chat options; for an immediate physical safety threat or medical emergency, the service directs people to call 911.

unresolved.text: No publicly available final law-enforcement or medical-examiner finding on Mitte’s cause and manner of death was located in the consulted sources.

related_stories.summary: A passenger train derailment near Multan, Pakistan, has resulted in at least five deaths and over 30 injuries. The incident involved the Rehman Baba Express and occurred early on October 13. Authorities have initiated an investigation to determine the cause of the accident.

related_stories.title: Supreme Court to Review Trump Administration's Case on DOGE Records
related_stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court has agreed to hear a case involving the Trump administration's claim that records related to Elon Musk's DOGE are exempt from Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requirements. The administration argues that DOGE qualifies as a presidential advisory body, thus limiting public access to its records.

related_stories.title: Fatal Incident on Six Flags Roller Coaster Leads to Ride Closures
related_stories.summary: A man named Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem was killed after being ejected from the 'Goliath' roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia. He reportedly struck other patrons during his fall before landing below. Following this incident, Six Flags announced the temporary closure of nine other roller coasters across its parks in North America as a precautionary measure. The incident is currently under investigation.
